wu: Weather Charades: Teacher mimes actions like shivering, sweating, or using an umbrella; students guess 'It's cold/hot/rainy' in full sentences. Teacher writes correct sentences on the board.
wuAlt: Weather Bingo: Students draw 9 weather symbols, teacher calls out 'It's sunny/rainy...' and students mark the matching symbol.
Weather Chain: One student says 'I like sunny weather', next says 'I like sunny weather and I like snowy weather', etc.
pres: Teacher shows flashcards of different weather and asks 'What is the weather like?'; models answers 'It's sunny/rainy/snowy'. Then shows a calendar with 'Saturday' and asks 'What are you going to do on Saturday?'; models answers 'I'm going to play football/watch TV'.
presAlt: Weather Report Video: Play a short cartoon weather forecast, pause and ask students to report the weather using the target language.
Plan Your Day: Teacher draws a simple timeline of their Saturday and says 'I'm going to wake up at 8, I'm going to have breakfast...', students repeat.
prac: Weather and Plans Matching: Students have cards with weather on one side and activities on the other; they match them and make sentences like 'It's sunny, I'm going to the park'. Teacher monitors and corrects.
pracAlt: Find Someone Who...: Students walk around and ask 'What are you going to do this weekend?'; find someone who matches each activity and write their name.
Picture Prompt: Students get a picture of a weather scene and must tell their partner what they are going to do in that weather.
ls: Listen to two friends making weekend plans; students complete a table with 'Name' and 'Plan' (e.g., 'Lina: going to the cinema'). Teacher plays the audio twice, then checks answers as a class.
re: Weather TPR: Teacher calls out weather commands like 'If it's sunny, jump! If it's rainy, cover your head!', students act them out quickly to reactivate vocabulary.
prod: Christmas Party Planning: In groups, students plan a Christmas party with a 500-dirham budget. They must decide on food, games, and decorations using 'We're going to buy... We're going to play...'. Each group presents their plan.
rw: Christmas Around the World Jigsaw: Students read short texts about Christmas in different countries (e.g., USA, UK, Morocco). They then share one fact from their text with a partner and write a sentence about it.
st: Teacher tells a short story about a character's Christmas plans, using target language. End with 'Today we learned to talk about weather and make plans. Thank you, class!'
g: Students mime weather actions for others to guess in sentences.
Students write their weekend plans on paper and swap with a partner to ask questions.
Students mark off party items as the teacher calls them out.
Students ask classmates about weekend plans and find matches.
Teacher says 'Sunny weather is better than rainy weather'; students go to corners and defend their choice.
diff: Fast finishers: Design a dream Christmas party with no budget limit and present it to the class.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'I'm going to...' and 'It's...' for the party planning task.
hw: Write a 6-8 sentence paragraph about the weather in Oujda this weekend and what you are going to do.
Write a 10-line invitation to a class Christmas party, including the date, time, and activities.
Draw a picture of your weekend plans and write 5 sentences about it using 'going to'.
tip: Use local context: Discuss how Moroccans celebrate Christmas (family gatherings, special foods) to make the theme relevant and build cultural awareness.
